disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.body: Symply is an educational tool for tracking foods and symptoms related to histamine intolerance. It is not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Food classifications are approximate and can vary from person to person. Consult a doctor or dietitian for health decisions.

mechanism.daoExplain: Diamine oxidase (DAO) is the main enzyme that breaks down dietary histamine in the gut. A "DAO inhibitor" is a substance that lowers this enzyme’s activity (e.g. alcohol), so histamine is cleared more slowly and builds up — even low-histamine food can then worsen symptoms.
mechanism.liberatorExplain: Liberators trigger the release of histamine stored in the body’s own cells (mast cells), regardless of how much histamine the food itself contains. The result is a rise in body histamine and symptoms similar to eating histamine (e.g. citrus, strawberries).
